where: crates/blaze-lints/src/check.rs (upmap), a lint of expressions inside macro arguments
what: An expression written in a macro call argument (`id!(a + 1)`) did not map back to the file: the node range of a `$e:expr` fragment includes the invisible group tokens, which carry the macro definition spans, so `Cx::upmap` refused the whole range as made up by the macro and the finding was dropped silently.
cause: upmap asks every span of the range to share one anchor; the splice adds tokens of another
workaround: Cx::written_range trims the macro-context spans off both ends before requiring one anchor
state: fixed for implicit_overflow; other lints that use Cx::range on fragment expressions still drop them
